Welcome to our school
Durdans Park Primary School is a two form entry community school with a large nursery set in extensive grounds.
The school values of Equality, Excellence and Enjoyment underpin all aspects of school life. We pride ourselves on being a welcoming and nurturing school and working in harmony with the wider community.
We are committed to supporting children to meet their full potential allowing all to flourish.
Our pupils behave well and have an enthusiasm for learning. Everything the school does focusses upon providing the best educational experience for pupils with a rich curriculum and an engaging range of wider curriculum experiences.

pageCache.pageTitle: Aims & Visions - Durdan's Park Primary School
pageCache.text:
Mission Statement
Children learn best when happy. Their environment must be as happy and supportive as possible. An environment they enjoy being in and can see the value of their learning. An environment parents feel valued and trusted, and where their parents and governors feel confident that the children are receiving the best possible start to their formal education.
Vision Statement
We focus on developing staff knowledge and expertise to provide the best start to a child's educational journey. We deliver an engaging deep and broad curriculum, with a wealth of extra-curricular experiences that are enriching and inspirational.
CORE VALUES
How we do it - Our values describe the approach to teaching and learning which we use to develop pupils and prepare them for future life.
EQUALITY
Instil Equality - our pupils will have equal opportunities to succeed. When they need additional help and support it will be provided. They will have opportunities to excel. They will learn to manage their own thinking and well-being and work effectively with others.
EXCELLENCE
Developing Excellence - our pupils will strive to be the best they can, always challenging themselves to do better within a secure and supportive learning environment. They will gain the powers of analysis and problem solving in each subject.
ENJOYMENT
Secure Enjoyment - our pupils will leave with an understanding that learning is fun and the opportunities they have received at Durdan’s Park have provided meaningful enhancement to their lives.

pageCache.text:
Curriculum Enhancements
KIT Theatre
Our children all have opportunities, throughout their time at Durdans Park, to take part in immersive theatre which brings the stories they learn to life and deepens their understanding.
This is an integral part of our Oracy curriculum, providing the experience of working and performing with professional actors. The projects each year support critical thinking, dialogue, role play and collaboration, helping pupils articulate ideas and practice effective communication.
Primary Shakespeare Company
Primary Shakespeare Company brings Shakespeare’s plays to life, through drama, storytelling and performance, working alongside professional actors. It enhances pupil’s oracy by fostering speaking and listening skills and encouraging creative expression. This project is part of our year 4 curriculum, exposing pupils to the classic stories and Shakespearean language. Our pupils have the opportunity to perform, alongside other schools, in a real theatre. This provides an opportunity for performance but also critical review of others’ performance.
HeyDay UK
In year 5 our pupils have an opportunity to work alongside professional filmmakers. Our pupils are empowered to create their own films, working on scripting, filming and editing. It enhances pupils oracy and confidence by developing skills in storytelling, scriptwriting, collaborative discussions and performance. The project fosters creativity, confidence building and effective communication through the filmmaking process.
As part of our wonderful work with Heyday, pupils are invited to attend the British Film Institute (BFI) for an interschool short film festival. This event celebrates our achievements and budding filmmaking skills. Pupils are provided with a platform to speak about their films and the many diverse themes they encapsulate.
EveryDay Magic
Everyday Magic’s professional storytellers bring songs, rhymes and stories to life with our youngest children. It helps to develop children’s oracy, by developing active participation in storytelling and performance which builds confidence and develops language.The stories fire up imagination and excitement and introduce both familiar and new ideas.
Forest School Association
We run our Forest School on the fields, amongst the trees and plants on our school site. We have a trained member of staff on our team who runs weekly Forest School sessions for our children in year 1 and Reception. This programme supports play, exploration and supported risk taking. It develops confidence and self esteem through hands-on activities in the natural environment and is closely linked to our theme of sustainability as children are taught about how to look after our natural world.
Clubs
We have a wide range of clubs, which run after school every day. Many are linked to sports and fitness, led by sports specialist and leading to high achievement in sports.
Whilst our children are exposed to a wide range of sports and practice on sports’ fields with high quality equipment, our specialist sport is cricket and we have professional cricket nets for children to practice in. We are always looking for opportunities for our most talented pupils to develop their skills outside of school.
In addition, we have an after school and before school club and many additional “booster” classes to ensure pupils keep up academically.
Animal Care
Durdans Park has a school dog called Kenny. Children are taught about animals, their needs and behaviours. This develops a sense of care, responsibility and respect for the welfare of living things.
Children in Nursery and Reception have the opportunity to meet and learn about a wide range of farm animals during an annual mobile farm visit.
The school has a wild garden with bug hotels and wild flowers, to encourage a wide range of mini-beasts to take up residence. There are also many bird boxes around the school to provide a safe environment for nesting birds.
Bridge to Year 7
The school holds an annual aspiration day for year 6 pupils. This event provides an opportunity for pupils to meet and interview a diverse group of professionals who volunteer their time.
The aim of this event is to broaden pupils’ knowledge of different careers, raise their aspirations and develop an understanding of what skills each career requires. This event links to the theme of power.

pageCache.pageTitle: Modern Foreign Languages - Durdan's Park Primary School
pageCache.text:
Modern Foreign Languages (MFL)
At LMPS, we teach our KS2 pupils French and this is taught by a specialist teacher.
At Durdans Park, we believe that learning a modern foreign language is a powerful tool for developing confident, articulate, and culturally aware learners. Our French curriculum, rooted in the National Curriculum for Languages (KS2), aims to build strong foundations in language acquisition while fostering curiosity, respect, and intercultural understanding.
We are proud that French is taught by a specialist language teacher, ensuring high-quality, accurate language modelling and a rich, authentic experience for all pupils. Through engaging, progressive lessons, children develop the knowledge and confidence to understand and express themselves in French, while gaining a broader perspective of the world and their place within it.
Our ambition is that every child leaves Year 6 with a love of language learning, a secure grasp of French vocabulary and grammar and the cultural awareness to thrive as global citizens in an interconnected world.
Our French curriculum reflects the National Curriculum’s aims for pupils to:
The aims as outlined above are embedded in a progressive and structured scheme of work that promotes language proficiency through listening, speaking, reading, and writing.
Understanding Language Development
Our approach is grounded in the science of language learning. Research shows that early language exposure:
• Enhances cognitive flexibility, memory, and problem-solving.
• Supports metalinguistic awareness, strengthening literacy in both the first language and the new language.
• Improves phonological awareness, contributing to stronger reading and spelling outcomes.
We prioritise spoken language and listening in the early stages of KS2, progressing to reading and writing with grammatical awareness and application by Year 6. Sentence stems, repetition, and oracy routines help embed syntax, structure, and fluency.
Valuing Bilingualism
Many of our pupils at Durdans Park are already bilingual or multilingual. We celebrate this as a strength and draw on their lived experiences to make meaningful comparisons between languages.
We recognise that bilingual pupils may demonstrate:
• Enhanced listening skills and code-switching ability.
• Deep metalinguistic insight.
• Cultural empathy and international perspectives.
Our curriculum leverages these strengths, enabling all pupils—regardless of background—to thrive as language learners and contributors to our diverse school community.
• Inclusive and Ambitious: Every child can learn a language. Scaffolds, visuals, and modelled routines support all learners, including those with SEND or new to English.
• Culturally Enriching: We connect pupils with Francophone cultures across the world—France, Canada, Senegal, Haiti—to expand horizons and challenge stereotypes.
• Integrated with Whole School Learning: Cross-curricular links to geography, music, history, and literacy deepen understanding and reinforce vocabulary and context.
• Celebratory and Fun: Language learning is joyful. We celebrate achievements through assemblies, performances, French Days, and pen-pal exchanges.

pageCache.pageTitle: Personal Development - Durdan's Park Primary School
pageCache.text:
Personal development at Ealing Bridges Federation
Mental health
We understand that positive mental health is fundamental to our pupils overall wellbeing and success. That is why we prioritise mental health support at every step of our pupils’ journey. Through our partnership with the Schools Counselling Partnership and THRIVE, we provide a safe space for children to express themselves, process emotions, and develop coping strategies. We believe that by fostering a culture of openness and understanding, we can break down the stigma surrounding mental health and empower our pupils to prioritise their emotional wellbeing. Whether it is through one-on-one counselling sessions, group activities, or mindfulness exercises, we strive to instil resilience and promote a positive mindset in every child.
Rights Respecting
At our school, we aim to be a safe and inspiring place to learn, where children are respected, and their talents and nurtured, so they can thrive. By ensuring that the principles of the UN Convention on the Rights of the Child are woven into school through our ethos, we strive to create a nurturing and inclusive community where every child’s rights are respected, protected, and upheld.
Pupil voice
At our school, pupils are empowered to direct their own learning and voice their opinions. From creating and directing their own films to suggesting improvements to their lessons, children play an active role in shaping their educational experience. Through oracy-focused activities and rights-based language development, we foster a culture where children feel confident to speak up and advocate for themselves and others.
Our pupil leadership groups, including the Legacy, Morality, OPAL and Sustainability Ambassadors as well as Junior Leadership Team, play an integral role in shaping our school community. These groups empower children to make positive changes, from promoting sustainability initiatives to advocating for mental health awareness. Pupil voice is at the heart of our decision-making processes, with children actively involved in shaping our school development priorities and curriculum themes.
Inclusivity
Our commitment to diversity and inclusion is reflected in our curriculum, which is regularly reviewed and developed to represent the rich tapestry of our school community. Children with Special Educational Needs receive tailored support, ensuring that every child has the opportunity to reach their full potential.
Assemblies
Assemblies at our school serve as meaningful gatherings where our community comes together to celebrate achievements, reflect on values, and foster a sense of belonging. Each assembly serves a unique purpose tailored to support our pupils’ holistic development. Singing assemblies ignite joy and camaraderie as voices unite in song, uplifting spirits and nurturing a sense of togetherness. Headteacher assemblies provide opportunities for leadership, where students share updates, achievements, and inspirational messages, fostering a culture of responsibility and empowerment. Pastoral assemblies offer a space for reflection and support, addressing topics such as well-being, resilience, and kindness, equipping students with the tools to navigate life’s challenges with confidence and compassion. Race equality and diversity assemblies promote understanding and appreciation of different cultures, fostering an inclusive environment where every child feels valued and respected. Through these diverse assemblies, we not only cultivate a strong sense of community but also instil values that will guide our students to become compassionate, responsible, and respectful individuals, ready to make a positive impact on the world around them.
In summary, the federation is a nurturing community dedicated to holistic development. From promoting positive mental health and fostering inclusivity to upholding children’s rights and offering enriching programs like forest school and diverse assemblies, we aim to cultivate confident, resilient, and compassionate individuals. With the support of our staff and school community, we empower every child to thrive academically, emotionally, and socially, preparing them to make a positive impact in the world.
Part of Ealing Bridges Federation

pageCache.pageTitle: Rights Respecting School - Durdan's Park Primary School
pageCache.text:
Rights Respecting School
At Durdans Park Primary School, we are proud to be a Bronze: Rights Respecting School, awarded by UNICEF UK in recognition of our whole-school commitment to placing the United Nations Convention on the Rights of the Child (UNCRC) at the heart of everything we do.
A rights-based approach to education
We believe every child should:
Feel heard and valued
Learn in a safe, supportive environment
How we live our rights respecting ethos
Curriculum integration
Children explore the rights through our high-quality texts interwoven through our expertly planned curriculum. Some examples are:
Each class creates a Rights Charter at the beginning of the year, linking behaviour expectations to the UNCRC. These charters are central to classroom life and referred to in real-time to guide learning and interactions.
Pupil voice and leadership
Our Morality ambassadors work closely with staff to monitor how rights are promoted across the school. They:
Behaviour and wellbeing
We use a restorative approach rooted in the language of rights. This helps pupils reflect on their actions, understand their impact on others and resolve conflicts respectfully.
Whole school culture
Rights language is visible in every corridor, conversation and classroom. Our assemblies often focus on a key article, connecting global rights to local experiences. Staff model rights-respecting behaviour at all times.
Lead assemblies and campaigns
Gather feedback from peers
Gather and represent pupil views
The impact
As a result of our rights-based work, pupils at Durdans Park:
Speak with confidence about justice, equity, and fairness
Our Rights Respecting work contributes to a calm, purposeful climate for learning where every child feels safe, heard, and supported.
Working in partnership
We work closely with our families and wider community to promote and uphold rights beyond the school gates. Through newsletters, workshops and family projects, we ensure that the language of rights is shared and lived at home and in our neighbourhood.
Part of Ealing Bridges Federation

This does not include any extracurricular activities that a pupil may choose to participate in.

Science
The teaching of science at Durdans Park Primary School helps children to develop useful knowledge, skills and attitudes about the world we live in.
In the modern world in which we live today, science touches every part of our lives. Our future prosperity depends on scientific advances and yet we have a shortage of scientists.
At Durdans Park Primary School, we celebrate and promote science, both in science specific lessons, and across the curriculum. Our pupils share a sense of excitement and curiosity about the natural world in which we live.
They also develop the belief that if they are not sure about something, they should not accept it, but challenge and ask WHY?
Because all pupils are scientists, they answer the question why, by:
As a result, our curriculum is structured to ensure that our learning is developed through: observing, investigating and researching.
Our aim is pupils will be so inspired by Science at Durdans Park Primary School, they will become the greatly needed scientists of tomorrow.
Science curriculum follows the National Curriculum themes and requirements, whilst also linking to our class topics so as to provide a meaningful context for learning.
Science is covered in the Foundation Stage through ‘Understanding the World’. Here, pupils explore and investigate the natural world as well as themselves.
Throughout Key stages 1 and 2, key learning is reinforced and developed through a combination of: investigation, experimentation, research and observation.
Children are encouraged to question, predict and test their ideas through whole class, group or individual investigations and project work and then form conclusions. Thus developing a curiosity and a desire for learning.
As science is everywhere, this is reflected in our wider curriculum, which has many cross curricular links to science planned in.
Our commitment to science at Lady Margaret School is reflected in our investment of a specialist science teacher who both teaches and supports teachers in the delivery of science.
Science is not just limited to the classroom. During their time at Durdans Park, children widen their experiences by participating in educational visits. Examples of these include the Science Museum, the Wetland Centre, Kew Gardens and Odds Farm.
In addition, there are a number of after school clubs that pupils are able to attend. These are designed to enable pupils to have a greater input into what they study. For example, in one current club, pupils are combining their electrical, DT and programming skills to construct a haunted house that is wired up with motors, lights, and servos to create a variety of spooky effects.
All the pupils are involved in the development and running of our edible garden, which was a winner in ‘The Ealing in bloom award’. This develops a greater understanding of the life cycles of plant life, and also the importance of plants for us.
Early years also develop their understanding of the lifecycle each year, when they observe the hatching of chicks. Some of the chickens join the hens which reside by the wildlife garden. Once again the pupils are encouraged to visit and observe our chickens, who are now quite tame.
Finally, we are developing an outdoor wildlife area to enable us to develop a better understanding of the wild life that is around us, that we are often not aware of.
Our aim is pupils will be so inspired by Science at Ealing Bridges Federation they will become the greatly needed scientists of tomorrow.
When our pupils move on to High School we hope that many of them will continue in their studies of science.
Our pupils will have:
…developed a love and passion for the subject.
…have a good scientific knowledge and conceptual understanding of science.
…have the confidence and ability to carry out, and report on, science enquiries that help them to answer scientific questions about the world around them.
…be equipped with scientific knowledge required to understand the uses and implications of science, today and for the future.
…use their scientific knowledge and understanding to care for the world in which they live.

The School Governors
Our governors are at the heart of how the school operates.If you want to contact the chair of governors or any other governor please leave a message or a letter at the school office and your request will be passed on to the relevant governor.
The Role of the Governing Body
All maintained schools in England have a governing board which is responsible for overseeing the strategic direction of the school. A key role is to act as a ‘critical friend’: to support, to challenge, and to ask questions.
The governing board works in close partnership with the Interim Executive Headteacher and the Local Authority to ensure the school functions well and offers a strong provision for the education of the children it serves.
Membership of the governing board includes parents, teaching staff and representatives from the local community and the Local Authority.
The governing board has a range of powers and duties laid down by various Education Acts. In the main, these responsibilities relate to:
Governors adopt, review and monitor a range of statutory policies that govern the operation of the school. These policies can be found on this website.
Governors discharge the above responsibilities through two formal governing board meetings each term. In addition, they make termly visits during the school day to monitor the impact of school improvement priorities.
Minutes of meetings are agreed and approved by the board at its next meeting. Minutes are available on request once they have been approved. Please contact the school administration team.
A number of governors also have responsibilities for specific areas within the school. The Terms of Reference outline the specific responsibilities of the governing body.
Management of the school’s budget
Instrument of Government
The instrument of government is the document that records the name of the school and the constitution of its governing board.
Instrument of Government – Ealing Bridges Federation.
Skills required of school governors
The National Governance Association (NGA) has published a list of skills required for school governance. An individual governor is not expected to have all the skills listed in the audit, but they should be covered across the governing body:
Governors Register of Interests
Governors have a legal duty to act in the best interest of the school. Where there are personal or financial interests, which may conflict with this duty, they must identify, prevent and record the conflict. Governors must not be involved in discussions or vote on matters to which their conflict relates.
At Durdan’s Park, governors review a register of interests at the start of every meeting. Governors also declare personal or other interests which might be a potential source of conflict. Please click on the link below for the most up to date register of business interests.

School Clubs
We aim to nurture pupils talents and interests through a range of after school activities which run across the federation. We are vigilant in identifying pupils who would benefit from a particular aspect of the provision and ensure opportunities are not missed due to particular needs and circumstances.
Breakfast Club
A breakfast club runs daily at Durdans Park Primary from 8:00 – 8:45, led by Ms Mangat, for children of working parents. Parents must book in advance through their Magic Booking account.
After school childcare provision
An after school club runs daily from 3:15 to 4:30, led by Mrs Neville, for children of working parents. Children take part in a range of indoor and outdoor learning activities and are provided with a small healthy snack. Parents must book in advance through their Magic Booking account.
After school sports clubs
We offer a variety of sports clubs which cost £4.50 per session and run from 3.30pm to 4.30pm. Children are escorted to the club by two members of staff. Parents can book a place on clubs for their child/ren through their Magic Booking account.
Clubs begin Monday 14th September and run until Friday 11th December.

pageCache.pageTitle: Art and Design - Durdan's Park Primary School
pageCache.text:
Art & Design
Art and design is an important foundation subject and is taught and experienced throughout school linked to the topics. It is used not only as a form of communication but also as a form of expression.
As artists, we explore some of the highest forms of creativity. We design, craft and invent our own art work using knowledge and skills. We understand the importance of art in history and culture and study famous artists and their importance.
‘Every child is an artist. The problem is how we remain an artist when we grow up’
At Durdans Park Primary School, we teach Art and Design as a discrete subject that link to either the core text, or the focus topic for that half term (geography or history). This makes the learning memorable, meaningful and enjoyable while simultaneously developing a breadth of study of artistic knowledge and skills.
The learning journey in Art and Design consists of the following:
• A discussion around famous quotes made by a range of artists
• An introduction of the topic and the idea/activity
• An analyses of the focus artists’ pieces where the children immerse themselves into the world of visual language and representation
• A demonstration of the focus process or technique delivered by experiences teachers
• The children creating their own pieces using either the artist influence, process or stimulus that they resonated with
• An evaluation and reflection of their own pieces
Our Art and Design curriculum, starting from the Early Years foundation stage up to Key Stage 2, is a culturally rich plan in order to expose our children to art in the wider world.
Our curriculum coverage allows for a breadth of opportunities such as the engagement in an artists in residence programme, Legacy Project and cultural week. Durdans Park Primary School serves a diverse community of many cultures and languages. We want all our children to gain knowledge and understanding of the art from around the world.
Throughout the academic year, our children have opportunities to further develop their understanding of artic knowledge and skills through other subjects such as PSHE (anti-bullying week), Reading (Book week), Religious Studies (Spirited arts competition) and much more.

pageCache.pageTitle: Attendance Procedures - Durdan's Park Primary School
pageCache.text:
Attendance Procedures
Attend Today, Achieve Tomorrow.
Attendance Matters – Statistics show a direct link between poor attendance and under-achievement.
Regular attendees
Absence for whatever reason disadvantages a child by creating gaps in his/her learning. A good understanding of the work and good progress can only take place when the child is in the classroom regularly and on time.
Durdans Park Primary School has an attendance target of 96.1%. Each week the attendance for each class will be published in the newsletter. Children who have 100% attendance for the whole school year will be presented with a certificate to celebrate their achievement.
School registers are checked regularly by the head of school, assistant heads of school and the class teachers, and poor attendance is followed up. Each half term we are visited by an educational social worker from the Local Authority. They will review the attendance of all the children and may call a meeting with families where the absence rate is poor or where children have incomplete weeks of schooling. The following process is followed where there are concerns.
make better progress, both socially and academically
Stage 1
As soon as a child’s attendance falls below 96% a reminder letter is sent to the parent advising them that their child’s attendance must improve and that their attendance will be closely monitored.
Stage 2
Where a child’s attendance falls below 90%, the parent will be invited to attend a meeting with the pastoral assistant headteacher who will set a target for improvement. At this stage the parents will be advised that they may be referred to the education social work service if targets aren’t met
Stage 3
Where a child’s attendance fails to improve, the parent will be invited to attend a meeting with the headteacher who will set a target for improvement. At this stage the parents will be advised that they will be referred to the education social work service if targets aren’t met.
Stage 4
Where a child’s attendance target is not met the parents/carers will be referred to the local authority’s education social work service.
We expect parents to contact the school office by telephone every day that a child is away. There is a special line where you can leave messages about attendance and the messages will be picked up regularly.
Attendance Procedure Flowchart
Persistent Absenteeism Flowchart
Unauthorised Absence
There is no entitlement to time off during term time.
If children are absent for reasons, which are not permitted by law, or where the explanation or reason for the absence is considered unsatisfactory absence will be recorded as ‘unauthorised’.
We expect parents to contact the school office by telephone every day that a child is away. There is a special line where you can leave messages about attendance and the messages will be picked up regularly.
Examples of unauthorised absence are:
If a child goes abroad during a school holiday period, the parent must make definite arrangements so that they return in good time for school re-opening.
Absence claimed for unexpected delays will require documentary evidence together with proof of original return dates.
For example where illness prevents travel a doctor’s certificates must be provided (these should be in English) and must be accompanied by a travel ticket with dates that would have indicated a timely return.
If a child remains abroad at the beginning of a school term and absence extended parents will be advised that their child’s school place may be at risk.
It is an offence under section 444 of the Education Act 1996. “If a child of compulsory school age who is a registered pupil at a school fails to attend regularly at the school, his parent is guilty of an offence.”
If you take your child out of school without authorisation the school has the power to issue Fixed-Penalty Notices of £80, rising to £160 if not paid within 28 days and it should be noted that penalties may be issued to each parent for each child.

pageCache.pageTitle: Charging and Remission Policy - Durdan's Park Primary School
pageCache.text:
Charging and Remission Policy
This policy supports the Rights Respecting principles adopted by Durdans Park Primary School and is particular relevant to the following articles:
Article 3The best interests of the child must be a top priority in all things that affect children.
Article 15Every child has the right to meet with other children and to join groups and organisations, as long as this does not stop other people from enjoying their rights.
Article 27Every child has the right to a standard of living that is good enough to meet their physical, social and mental needs. Governments must help families who cannot afford to provide this.
Article 28Every child has the right to an education. Primary education must be free. Secondary education must be available for every child. Discipline in schools must respect children’sdignity. Richer countries must help poorer countries achieve this.
Article 29Education must develop every child’s personality, talents and abilities to the full. It must encourage the child’s respect for human rights as well as respect for their parents, their own and other cultures, and the environment.
Article 31Every child has the right to relax, play and take part in a wide range of cultural and artistic activities.
Introduction
The federation governing body recognises the valuable contribution that the wide range of additional activities including clubs and trips, can make towards pupils’ personal and social education and will wherever possible ensure that each child goes on a trip or has a visitor to class each term.
The governing body aims to promote such activities both as part of a broad balanced curriculum for the pupils and as additional optional extras.
We believe that all our pupils should have an equal opportunity to benefit from school activities and visits (curricular and extra-curricular) independent of their parents’/carers’ financial means.
This policy describes how we will do our best to ensure a good range of visits and activities is offered and, at the same time, try to minimise the financial barriers which may prevent some pupils taking full advantage of the opportunities.
Sections 449-462 of the Education Act 1996 set out the law on charging for school activities in schools maintained by local authorities in England.
The governing body of Ealing Bridges Federation have, determined that the school may make charges and seek voluntary contributions from parents for school activities provided for registered pupils at the school on the basis of the information set out in the main part of this document.
Aims
The Ealing Bridges Federation aims to:
Legislation and guidance
This policy is based on advice from the Department for Education (DfE) on charging for school activities and the Education Act 1996, sections 449-462 of which set out the law on charging for school activities in maintained schools in England.
It’s also based on guidance from the DfE on statutory policies for schools and academy trusts.
Definitions
Roles and responsibilities
The governing board has overall responsibility for approving the charging and remissions policy, but can delegate this to a committee, an individual governor or the ExecutiveHeadteacher.
The governing board also has overall responsibility for monitoring the implementation of this policy.
For the schools in our federation, monitoring the implementation of this policy has been delegated to the Chair of Governors.
The Executive Headteacher
The Executive Headteacher is responsible for ensuring staff are familiar with the charging and remissions policy, and that it is being applied consistently.
Our staff are responsible for:
– Implementing the charging and remissions policy consistently.– Notifying the Executive Headteacher of any specific circumstances which they are unsure about or where they are not certain if the policy applies.
The senior leadership team will provide staff with appropriate training in relation to this policy and its implementation.
Parents are expected to notify staff or the Executive Headteacher of any concerns or queries regarding the charging and remissions policy.
Where charges cannot be made
Below we set out what the school cannot charge for:
Admission applications
The national curriculum
Religious education
The national curriculum
Religious education
Where charges can be made
Below we set out what the school can charge for.
Optional extras (see below)
Music and vocal tuition, in limited circumstances
Certain early years provision
Community facilities
Optional extras
We are able to charge for activities known as ‘optional extras’. In these cases, the schools can charge for providing materials, books, instruments or equipment. The following are optional extras:
Education provided outside of school time that is not part of:
Transport (other than transport that is required to take the pupil to school or to other premises where the local authority/governing board has arranged for the pupil to be provided with education)
Board and lodging for a pupil on a residential visit
Extended day services offered to pupils (such as breakfast clubs, after-school clubs, tea and supervised homework sessions)
When calculating the cost of optional extras, an amount may be included in relation to:
Any charge made in respect of individual pupils will not be greater than the actual cost of providing the optional extra activity, divided equally by the number of pupils participating.
Any charge will not include an element of subsidy for any other pupils who wish to take part in the activity but whose parents are unwilling or unable to pay the full charge.
In cases where a small proportion of the activity takes place during school hours, the charge cannot include the cost of alternative provision for those pupils who do not wish to participate.
Parental agreement is necessary for the provision of an optional extra which is to be charged for.

Music tuition
The school can charge for vocal or instrumental tuition provided either individually or to groups of pupils, provided that the tuition is provided at the request of the pupil’s parent.
Charges may not exceed the cost of the provision, including the cost of the staff giving the tuition.
Charges cannot be made:
Residential visits
We can charge for board and lodging on residential visits, but the charge must not exceed the actual cost.
Voluntary contributions
As an exception to the requirements set out in section 5 of this policy, the school is able to ask for voluntary contributions from parents to fund activities which would not otherwise be possible.
Some activities for which the school may ask parents for voluntary contributions include:
There is no obligation for parents to make any contribution, and no child will be excluded from an activity if their parents are unwilling or unable to pay.
If the school is unable to raise enough funds for an activity or visit then it will be cancelled.
If the activity is cancelled all monies paid will be returned to parents/carers.
Any voluntary contribution asked for in respect of an activity or visit will not exceed the total cost to the school divided equally by the number of pupils participating. It will therefore never include any element of subsidy for any other pupils wishing to participate in the activity whose parents/carers are unwilling or unable to contribute the full amount.
The federation is committed to ensuring fair access and treatment of all pupils, and this means ensuring that no pupil is excluded from an activity because the parents/carers of that pupil are unwilling or unable to pay. If there is insufficient funding for an activity, then it will be cancelled. The identity of the pupil or parents/carers of the pupil who did not want to make the payment, or could not make the payment, will not be disclosed under any circumstances.
The federation often subsidises some of the day trip costs in order to support a visit.

The Governing Body may wish to remit in full or in part the cost of other activities for particular groups of parents, for example, in the case of family hardship. When arranging a chargeable activity such parents will be invited in confidence for the remission of charges in full or in part. Authorisation for such remission will be made by the Executive Headteacher in consultation with the Chair of Governors.
